newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Commercial oil transit deal ready-Russia's Nemtsov.
newsitem.headline: Commercial oil transit deal ready-Russia's Nemtsov.

text.p: A commercial deal between oil firms in Russia, Chechnya and Azerbaijan on transporting early oil from an Azeri-based consortium could be signed soon, Russian Fuel and Energy Minister Boris Nemtsov was quoted by Interfax news agency as saying on Friday.
"We are ready to sign this agreement now, but there were no representatives from the Chechen side in Moscow today, and therefore the deal has yet to be concluded," Nemtsov said.
Interfax quoted Azeri President Haydar Aliyev as saying that the three-sided deal on transporting early Caspian oil through the pipeline was of a purely "commercial" character.
He stressed that it would be Russian, Chechen and Azeri oil companies which are to sign the deal.
Signing the agreement by companies and not states appears to represent a workable compromise to avoid the thorny issue of sovereignty blocking the agreement further.
Independence-minded Chechnya wanted high transit fees and a greater managing role, but Moscow said this was inappropriate since Chechnya was a part of Russia.
The companies due to sign the deal were Russia's oil pipeline monopoly Transneft, Chechnya's Southern Oil Company (YUNKO) and Azerbaijan's state oil company SOCAR.

Nemtsov said that repairing the oil pipeline crossing the territory of Chechnya would take around 20 days, and that early oil could pass along the route within a month of the commercial deal being signed.
The Azerbaijan International Operating Company (AIOC) oil consortium plans to start output from fields in the Azeri section of the Caspian Sea in August.
It wants to ship early oil from the $8 billion project through an existing pipeline which runs from the Azeri capital of Baku to the Russian Black Sea export outlet of Novorossiisk.
About 160 km of the nearly 1,500 km pipeline runs through Chechnya, passing through the war-ravaged city of Grozny.
